note: Thursday 07:00 SGT, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Wed 29 Jul US close — FOMC DECISION DAY. The dominant shifts: (1) the Fed held at 3.50-3.75% but HAWKISHLY — a 9-3 vote with three dissents wanting a hike, a terse statement and Warsh's 'won't hesitate' tone — and stocks sold off hard (Dow -2.19%, worst day since Apr 2025); (2) the US-Iran pause BROKE overnight and oil ripped +7-8% (Brent ~$90.7). 8 of 12 items are dated Wed 29 Jul (last 24h). Every item source-verified. Thu 30 Jul brings Q2 GDP/core-PCE (8:30am ET) and AAPL/AMZN earnings after the close.

items.headline: Fed delivers a HAWKISH hold: 9-3 with three dissents for a hike; Warsh 'won't hesitate' on inflation
items.summary: The FOMC held the target range at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting, but the decision read hawkish: the vote was 9-3 with three regional-president dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) preferring an immediate 25bp hike. Chair Kevin Warsh issued a deliberately short statement, gave no September commitment, and said the Fed 'won't hesitate' to stop inflation — framing prices, not the labor market, as the policy driver. There was no SEP. Markets judged the Fed to be 'behind' on inflation.
items.actionable: The hawkish hold with three hike dissents is the direct headwind for levered silver and SGX REITs — the 10Y jumped ~7bp to ~4.64% and the dollar firmed. Keep the big USD cash pile (~3.5-3.75%) as productive dry powder; the September meeting is now a live hike risk, so hedge the rate-sensitive book rather than adding leverage into it.

items.headline: Stocks sell off hard on the hawkish hold: Dow -2.19% (worst day since Apr 2025), VIX +13% to 20.66
items.summary: US equities fell sharply after the FOMC decision: the Dow dropped 2.19% (~1,150 points) to 51,594 — its worst day since April 2025 — the S&P 500 -1.52% to 7,316.15, the Nasdaq -1.74% to 24,443 and the Russell 2000 -1.61%. The VIX jumped 13.45% to 20.66. Industrials (-3.4%) and tech (-2.4%) led the drop; energy was the lone gaining sector on the oil spike. Long yields rose as the bond market signaled the Fed is falling behind on inflation.
items.actionable: A broad risk-off that hit everything rate-sensitive the book cares about (S-REITs, metals miners, HK tech beta) except energy. With BofA FMS cash at just 3.6% (contrarian sell), the stretched-bullish positioning amplified the drop — the productive cash pile is the hedge and the dry powder for redeploying after the shakeout resolves. Watch Thu GDP/PCE and AAPL/AMZN for whether the selloff extends.

items.headline: US-Iran pause BREAKS: oil spikes ~+8% (Brent ~$90.7, WTI ~$84.5) on renewed strikes and Red Sea attacks
items.summary: The US-Iran fighting pause that had held since ~27 Jul collapsed on Wednesday: renewed airstrikes, Trump warning Iran 'is going to get a beating' after repeated tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthis declaring a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia with two claimed Red Sea tanker strikes. Brent surged ~7.9% to ~$90.74 and WTI ~6.6% to ~$84.46, reversing the prior week's slide and re-inflating the war/inflation premium.
items.actionable: A double-edged shock: the oil spike re-arms the inflation/rate-hike fear that pressures the rate-sensitive book (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech, crypto) right as the Fed turned hawkish, but it also restores the geopolitical safe-haven bid under gold/silver and lifts the small energy long. Net: keep gold-heavy GDX as the hedge; the reignited Hormuz risk is now the key cross-portfolio swing factor again.

items.headline: Silver and gold hold as havens through the selloff — silver ~$57.5, gold ~$4,029 above $4,000
items.summary: Precious metals were resilient on FOMC day: silver held roughly flat at ~$57.5/oz and gold at ~$4,029 (above the $4,000 line), gaining modestly after the hold as the reignited Middle East conflict and the equity selloff drew a safe-haven bid that offset a firmer dollar. Silver's structural case is intact (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit; JPMorgan ~$81 avg target). GDX sat near $74.2 (Tue close; Wed settle not cleanly pinned).
items.actionable: The levered silver core held up where equities fell — the oil-spike/geopolitical bid and haven demand cushioned the hawkish-Fed dollar headwind. Structurally the deficit thesis is the anchor; near-term, silver is caught between a hawkish Fed (bearish) and a reignited war premium (bullish), so the tape stays two-sided — hold the core, hedge the silver-vs-gold spread rather than chase.

items.headline: Semis rout extends: SMH -4%, >$1trn wiped since 24 Jul, Nasdaq 100 in correction
items.summary: The AI-chip selloff deepened on Wednesday: the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) fell ~4%, extending a ~9% one-month drop, and more than $1 trillion has been wiped from global semi/AI-hardware market caps between the 24 Jul close and 29 Jul (NVDA/SK Hynix/Samsung/Micron ~$700B of it). The Nasdaq 100 slipped into a ~10% correction from its June peak. Fears center on AI overcapacity (Meta's surplus-capacity 'Meta Compute' plan) and leverage-/margin-driven selling; Samsung posted +1,800% y/y profit yet fell 7%.
items.actionable: A deepening, portfolio-specific headwind for the chip leg of the HK-tech core (SMIC/0981.HK) — the AI-overcapacity narrative is now a valuation-regime shift, not a one-day scare. Continue favoring the internet/consumer names (Tencent, Xiaomi) over pure-semi exposure; watch AAPL/AMZN (Thu) capex commentary for whether the rout stabilizes or cascades further into Asia.

items.headline: Microsoft beats and pops +3% AH (Azure +43%); Meta beats but falls -7% AH on AI-capex
items.summary: The first leg of the mega-cap gauntlet split after Wednesday's close. Microsoft beat — Q4 FY26 revenue ~$90B (+18% y/y), Azure +43%, commercial RPO +84% — and rose ~3% after hours as a lower-than-feared near-term capex read reassured. Meta beat on the top and bottom line (Q2 revenue $60.8B, +28% y/y) but fell ~7% after hours as its elevated FY26 capex guide ($125-145B) reignited AI-spending-payback worries. Apple and Amazon report Thursday after the close.
items.actionable: The split verdict — MSFT rewarded for capex discipline, META punished for capex growth — is the crux of the AI-overcapacity debate now driving the semis rout and, by read-through, the SMIC chip leg. It argues for the software/platform layer over the hardware layer; keep Tencent/Xiaomi favored over pure-semi HK exposure. AAPL/AMZN Thu are the next test.

items.headline: Crypto stalls post-Fed: Bitcoin ~$64k, Ether ~$1,905 (+1.5%), Solana ~$74; Fear & Greed 29
items.summary: Crypto was resilient-to-flat through the FOMC risk-off: Bitcoin held around $64,000 (~+0.2%), Ether firmed to ~$1,905 (+1.5% vs Tue) and Solana ~$74 (+1%), diverging modestly from the equity selloff. The crypto Fear & Greed index sat at ~29 ('Fear'), little changed. With no crypto-specific catalyst, the market continues to trade as a risk-appetite barometer off the macro rate channel; the hawkish hold capped upside but the oil/geopolitical bid and a softer-than-feared capex read cushioned it.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto is the cleanest read on the risk-appetite impulse — its resilience while equities fell suggests the selloff was rate-driven rather than a broad liquidity flush. Treat it as a barometer: a further hawkish repricing into September pressures both crypto and the metals/REIT rate-sensitivity trade; a dovish data surprise (Thu PCE) would relieve both.

items.headline: Big data Thursday: Q2 GDP and core PCE (8:30am ET) plus AAPL/AMZN earnings — the post-Fed test
items.summary: Thursday 30 Jul brings the week's heaviest macro slate right after the hawkish hold: Q2 advance GDP (consensus ~+2.3% annualized), June core PCE (consensus ~+0.1% m/m, ~+3.3% y/y — the Fed's key inflation gauge) and weekly jobless claims (prior 187K), all at 8:30am ET. Apple and Amazon then report after the close, closing out the mega-cap earnings gauntlet. A hot PCE would validate the three FOMC hike dissents and pressure rate-sensitives further; a cool print would relieve them.
items.actionable: The PCE print is the immediate binary for the rate-sensitive book — a hot number extends the hawkish-Fed pressure on levered silver and S-REITs and lifts September hike odds; a cool one caps the yield backup and lets metals/REITs stabilize. AAPL/AMZN capex commentary is the read-through to the AI/semis complex and the SMIC leg. Let the prints resolve before redeploying the cash pile.

items.headline: Tencent suspends its buyback into a 30-day blackout ahead of 12 Aug results; HK internet had led
items.summary: Tencent halted its near-daily share repurchase program from ~22 Jul, entering the customary 30-day blackout window ahead of its 12 August interim results (it had bought ~1.1M shares for HK$500.7M on 9 Jul and run buybacks near-daily since mid-May under the 10% AGM mandate). The pause removes a mechanical corporate bid just as the HK-tech tape faces the global chip rout — though the internet names (Tencent, Alibaba, Xiaomi) had been decoupling from the semis weakness and drew a record China equity inflow the prior week.
items.actionable: The buyback blackout temporarily lifts a support under Tencent into a jittery tape and its 12 Aug print — a reason not to add aggressively before results, even as the internet sleeve stays the preferred HK-tech core over the SMIC chip leg. Xiaomi's own buyback (3.9M shares/HK$100.7M on 15 Jul) continues. Watch the 12 Aug earnings as the next catalyst.

items.headline: China Politburo delivers firmer H2 stimulus tone; record weekly China equity inflow (+$21.3bn) follows
items.summary: The late-July Politburo readout carried stronger-than-expected wording — 'strengthen countercyclical measures with precision and force,' more policy options, and actively expanding domestic demand — after Q2 GDP slowed to 4.3%. The signal drew a record 3rd-largest weekly China equity inflow (+$21.3bn) and EM's 2nd-largest weekly haul ever (+$29.6bn, BofA/EPFR wk to 22 Jul), plus the biggest MLF liquidity injection in five months. Emphasis tilts to faster fiscal execution and tech (AI, quantum, advanced manufacturing).
items.actionable: The structural bid under the HK-tech core (Tencent, Xiaomi) and, at the margin, the China-exposed SGX name (CapitaLand China Trust) — a record China inflow confirming the Politburo signal. Note the flow snapshot pre-dates the 29 Jul global risk-off; watch the 31 Jul Flow Show and August policy detail for whether the China bid survives the selloff before adding.

items.headline: SGX REIT season constructive (Keppel DC REIT DPU +11.3%) but banks drag; DBS reports 6 Aug
items.summary: Keppel DC REIT posted 1H26 distributable income +18.5% y/y and DPU +11.3% to 5.714 cents on positive reversions and acquisitions — a constructive read-through as Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT and CapitaLand China Trust report. But the STI slipped as banks weighed (DBS ~S$73.95, UOB ~S$42.95, OCBC ~S$29.10); MPACT's latest DPU was softer (7.97 cents) and CLCT FY25 DPU fell 14.7% on the weaker China/retail sleeve. Singtel's S$2B value-realisation buyback and Capital Group's >5% Singtel stake are structural bids.
items.actionable: A firm datacentre-REIT print is a positive read-through for the S-REIT sleeve, but the hawkish Fed (10Y ~4.64%) and the oil-spike inflation risk are fresh headwinds for the whole rate-sensitive complex. The China-retail drag (CLCT DPU -14.7%) and softer bank guidance temper it. Watch DBS results 6 Aug and whether the post-FOMC yield backup pressures S-REIT valuations.

items.headline: Lynas produces first commercial-scale terbium outside China; DoD deal advances as 10 Nov MOFCOM cliff nears
items.summary: Lynas (LYC.AX) produced first separated terbium oxide at its Malaysia plant — the first commercial-scale terbium separation outside China — alongside a reported ~US$96M US DoD supply agreement (with an NdPr price floor). Meanwhile China's broad October-2025 MOFCOM rare-earth export controls remain SUSPENDED until 10 Nov 2026 (~3.5 months out), while MP Materials and USA Rare Earth remain on China's entity-specific dual-use control list (added 22 Jun). Trump's 20 Jul EO further bars adversary-sourced critical materials for defense contractors.
items.actionable: Structural Western-supply validation for the ex-China rare-earth watchlist (Lynas heavy-REE capability, MP's DoD backing, UUUU's NdPr build-out), but the 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff is the calendar catalyst: near-term pricing urgency stays eased, so accumulate MP/UUUU on weakness into a potential control snap-back rather than chase the strategic re-rate now.
